name: EXP-CLI-003 Make the light path light and enforce the load budgets
goal:
EXP-CLI-003 — Make the light path light, and make the load budgets enforced

(Numbering note: EXP-CLI-002 is skipped because that label already appears in the header comment of
tests/human-output-mode.test.js for the historical human-output work; reusing it would make two
different bodies of work answer to one name.)

WHERE THIS STARTS — CORRECTION OF RECORD
EXP-CLI-001 (2c13ca22fb8c4e6c) was marked completed at 103ee921 having landed only its Phase 1 audit
plus a Phase 0 output-contract unification (source commit 39f2243c). Its goal spanned five phases and
its ACCEPTANCE section was NOT satisfied. `expedition refine --id 2c13ca22fb8c4e6c` cannot annotate
it: "Expedition 2c13ca22fb8c4e6c is completed; cannot refine a terminal expedition" (LifecycleBlocked)
— which is EXP-LIFE-001 finding E, hit again from the other side. So the unmet criteria are restated
here as THIS expedition's acceptance criteria, and the ledger carries the correction forward
append-only instead of leaving a completion that reads as convergence. The full qualification is
already hashed into proof/expeditions/2c13ca22fb8c4e6c/attachments/evidence-2c13ca22.md §6 and §9.
`expedition complete` returned status ok because the gate verifies evidence presence and working-tree
state, not prose acceptance criteria — that gate gap is itself worth noting to whoever owns the
lifecycle (EXP-LIFE-001, 73c5c033360fecf3).

ALREADY TRUE — DO NOT REDO
  * One output contract. src/cli/usage.ts (COMMANDS = 33 verbs, PUBLIC_VOCABULARY, GLOBAL_OPTIONS,
    helpPayload/renderHelpText/printHelp with the TTY rule) and src/cli/version.ts
    (projectVersion/printVersion) are shared by entry.ts and synth.ts. All nine invocations of the
    measured surface — version, --version, -v, help, --help, -h, status, status --json,
    status --human — are byte-identical across both entry points with matching exit codes. Precedence
    is --json > --human > TTY, and help is the only verb whose default depends on the TTY.
  * src/cli/status-light.ts is the single status implementation, reached from both paths; cmdStatus
    delegates to runStatus() and no longer constructs a Logger. The duplicated copy is gone.
  * tests/loader-entrypoint.test.js is chained (segment #115 of 115) and carries nine byte-identity
    guards plus contract assertions on the envelope, --human and the 33-verb list. It was previously
    orphaned: green, never run, asserting a bare semver the shipped binary no longer printed.
  * Phase 1 audit result: across 347 src/**/*.ts there are exactly 5 module-scope process.cwd()
    captures, 0 module-scope process.env reads, 0 module-scope process.on() registrations. The 20
    top-level new Set/Map are immutable lookup tables and are benign.

THE FIVE THINGS LEFT
  1. Make the five import-time captures resolve per call, BEFORE making anything lazy:
     infra/event-store.ts:13 EVENT_LOG_FILE, infra/event-store.ts:14 EVENT_STREAM_DIR,
     infra/state-store.ts:12 STATE_FILE, infra/state-store.ts:13 SNAPSHOTS_DIR,
     infra/checkpoint-store.ts:11 CHECKPOINT_FILE. Laziness changes WHEN a module is first imported,
     so any verb that resolves roots or changes cwd later would otherwise observe paths captured from
     a different directory. This is the correctness hazard of the whole expedition, not the line count.
     Note locateEventLog(root) in src/infra/event-store.ts is already the single authority for
     event-log layout (segmented > partitioned-flat > legacy-file, never throws) and is the model.
  2. Slim status-light.js below its 134-module / 916 KB graph so the dispatcher approaches budget.
     It is 45% of the monolith's graph and is statically imported by entry.ts, which is why the
     "light" path is not light. explain-replay-light.js at 45 modules proves the target is reachable.
  3. Turn synth.ts dispatch into a verb -> loader registry with per-namespace dynamic imports
     (mission, expedition, ledger deliver/seal, explain, first-contact, task, repo, adapter,
     doctor/checkpoint, log, validate, governance). Extract the helper clusters ONCE into modules of
     their own so handlers move without duplicating them — duplication is exactly how entry.ts and
     synth.ts drifted apart in the first place:
       git / working tree: getWorkingTreeStatus, isWorkingTreeDirty, runGitSpawn,
         getUntrackedSourcePaths, existingAutoCommitPathspecs, isTrackedPath, isScratchFile,
         isNonSourcePath, getNonDerivedWorkingTreeStatus, collectDerivedStateFiles, isAutoCommitEnabled
       ceremony / auto-commit: markCeremony, installExitFlush, flushPendingCeremony,
         wrapHandleIntentWithCeremony, bootstrapWithCapabilities
       gates: gateDecision, printGateBlock
       telemetry / args: setAgentTelemetryFromFlags, parseArgs
     Largest modules loaded eagerly but not needed by the light path: synth.js 357 KB,
     explain-observability.js 41 KB, first-contact.js 40 KB, control/execution-gate.js 38 KB,
     discovery/projections/project-model-capability.js 33 KB, state/derived/build-derived-state.js 27 KB.
  4. Repoint tests/helpers/cli-harness.js:24 from dist/cli/synth.js at the shipped dispatcher, so the
     suite exercises bin.synth. Phase 0 made this safe for the nine-invocation surface; the census
     says which verbs must be proven equivalent BEFORE the switch (mission 427, expedition 394 —
     52% of all invocations are ceremony — bootstrap 118, first-contact 113, explain 112, init 71,
     status 60, alignment 38, task 34). In-process work after module load is median 55.8 ms /
     p90 188.2 ms, so the win is in loading, not in the handlers.
  5. Add the DERIVED load-budget guard: a test that recomputes the eager graph per entry point and
     re-measures the representative verbs, failing on regression, so re-monolithization is caught by
     a number rather than by a review. Prove it works with a deliberate temporary regression, then
     remove that regression and say so in the evidence.

  * dispatcher eager graph <= 25 modules / <= 150 KB.
  * no verb loads more than 40% of the total module graph unless its work genuinely requires it.
  * npm run test:all stays green (115 segments, 407 s at Phase 0) and no currently-green orphan turns
    red. All spawn call-sites pass unchanged except the harness path and the four source-path guards
    (tests/verify-engine, tests/artifact-policy, tests/governance-orchestration,
    tests/impact-analyzer), which reference src/cli/synth.ts BY PATH and must move with the code and
    never be deleted.
  * the load-budget guard fails when a handler is added to the dispatcher's eager graph.
  * synth verify ok; synth log / checkpoint / doctor still report real counts and layouts on this
    repository (at Phase 0: verify 6/6 ok, doctor 12/12 after --fix, 470 events, segmented layout).
  * dist-manifest, determinism and proof re-baselined deliberately, with the new file count and
    rootHash stated in the evidence rather than left to be discovered.

MEASUREMENT HONESTY — the rule this expedition must follow, learned in Phase 0
Wall-clock deltas in this 2-core sandbox are not trustworthy unless an untouched control invocation
is measured in the SAME session, and the control's drift bounds every claim. In the Phase 0 A/B the
control (entry.js explain replay, code untouched) moved +3.1 ms in one run and +8.0 ms in another
while the process floor swung 20-36 ms — larger than most deltas being measured — so Phase 0
deliberately published NO speed claim and reported deterministic module counts instead. Two further
traps, both hit and both recorded: cross-session baselines are not comparable (the floor moved
25.2 -> 36.4 ms between sessions), and a build-revert control must be probed behaviourally
(entry.js version prints a bare semver on the old build and "{" on the new) because a probe aimed at
synth.js cannot distinguish them. Prefer counts, bytes and module graphs — they are deterministic —
and treat any millisecond claim as guilty until a same-session control acquits it.

NON-GOALS
  * No further output-contract changes: the four operator decisions (JSON envelope for --version with
    --human for the bare string; no status INFO line on stderr from either path; TTY-aware help with
    --human/--json overrides; one unified 33-verb list) are settled and now guarded by tests.
  * Not shrinking core/bootstrap.js (170 modules / 1091 KB, 13 eager steps) — this makes it lazily
    REACHABLE so only verbs that need it pay for it; making it smaller is a separate lever.
  * Not the test inventory or file-ownership guard (EXP-TEST-005), not suite merging (EXP-TEST-002),
    not the sharded runner (EXP-TEST-003), not the logging/failure envelope (EXP-TEST-001), not
    explicit-environment fields (EXP-TEST-004).
  * Not the ledger lifecycle defects themselves (EXP-LIFE-001, 73c5c033360fecf3), though this
    expedition is a fresh instance of finding E and should be cited there.

SEQUENCING (operator decision, 2026-10-13): the monolith work runs BEFORE the testing-strategy work.
After this lands, EXP-TEST-002's merge arithmetic and EXP-TEST-003's speedup measurements must be
re-taken, because the per-process term they were implicitly optimizing changes by roughly 3x.
